contradictions.Statement1: Section 3 says the waterproofing membrane should be at least 4mm thick.
contradictions.Statement2: Section 7 says the waterproofing membrane must be 5mm thick.
contradictions.Reasoning: Different membrane thickness requirements are given in different sections of the document.

contradictions.Statement1: Section 3 requires the protection screed to achieve a minimum compressive strength of 30 N/mm² at 28 days.
contradictions.Statement2: Section 7 requires the protection screed to achieve a minimum compressive strength of 25 N/mm² at 28 days.
contradictions.Reasoning: The two sections give different minimum strength values for the same protection screed.

contradictions.Statement1: The Products section calls for a mesh size of 100mm × 100mm.
contradictions.Statement2: The Execution section calls for a mesh size of 150mm × 150mm.
contradictions.Reasoning: The mesh size specified in Products is different from the mesh size specified in Execution.

contradictions.Statement1: §1.02.4 says the Main Contractor shall provide fire watch for all torch-on operations.
contradictions.Statement2: §8.04.6 says the Waterproofing Subcontractor shall be solely responsible for providing fire watch.
contradictions.Reasoning: The document is unclear about who provides fire watch — one section says the Main Contractor, another says the Subcontractor.

contradictions.Statement1: Section 6 mentions a 10-year warranty for the waterproofing work.
contradictions.Statement2: Section 7.03 mentions a 15-year warranty for the bituminous waterproofing system.
contradictions.Reasoning: Two different warranty periods are given for what looks like the same scope of work (10 vs 15 years).

contradictions.Statement1: §7.01.2 requires the primer to cure for a minimum of 24 hours before the membrane is applied.
contradictions.Statement2: §8.03.2 requires the membrane to be applied within 4 hours of priming while the primer is still tacky.
contradictions.Reasoning: Different waiting times after primer application are given — 24 hours cure versus a 4-hour tacky window.

contradictions.Statement1: §4.03 sets a wind speed limit of 30 km/h for torch-applied works.
contradictions.Statement2: Other parts of the specification imply a different operational wind limit may apply during membrane installation activities.
contradictions.Reasoning: There is ambiguity in the document regarding the wind speed threshold above which torch-applied work must be suspended.

contradictions.Statement1: §4.02 limits substrate moisture content to 5% by weight as measured by a calibrated moisture meter.
contradictions.Statement2: §8.01.2 references substrate moisture content not exceeding 5% by weight at time of priming.
contradictions.Reasoning: Substrate moisture content is addressed in two different sections with potentially different intent — one for general membrane application and one specifically for priming — creating ambiguity for site personnel.

contradictions.Statement1: §3.02.1 specifies tensile strength of not less than 800 N/50mm in the longitudinal direction.
contradictions.Statement2: §3.02.1 specifies tensile strength of not less than 800 N/50mm in the transverse direction.
contradictions.Reasoning: The specification requires the same tensile strength value (800 N/50mm) in two different directions, which may not be physically achievable for a directionally reinforced polyester carrier.

contradictions.Statement1: §3.01.4 states the membrane shall remain stable under continuous service temperatures from -10°C to +80°C with no flow, blistering, or delamination.
contradictions.Statement2: The Execution section implies a narrower service temperature window during certain installation and curing conditions, particularly above 4 hours of direct sun exposure.
contradictions.Reasoning: The service temperature range stated in Performance may not be consistent with the Execution section's references to thermal protection during early curing.
